nodes.label: Case-Alias Symlinks
nodes.rationale: Avoids Wine's case-insensitive directory scans; measured load time 2:45 to 1:35 on a ~500-mod list.

nodes.label: Delivering MO2 refresh Under Proton
nodes.rationale: MO2's QSharedMemory and QLocalServer are named objects in the prefix's wineserver, so refresh reaches the running MO2 only when started in the same prefix with a compatible Wine.

nodes.rationale: On a default CachyOS install nothing is case-insensitive; every lookup in Data, mods and overwrite compares lower-cased relative paths and dedupes case-alias symlinks by realpath.

nodes.label: FormID
nodes.rationale: The hex value seen in game prefixes the load-order slot and moves with it; the identity (defining plugin plus local number) does not.

nodes.norm_label: link (record field pointing at a formid)

nodes.label: Guide
nodes.rationale: Served both as an MCP resource and through a tool, because the two reach different consumers.

nodes.label: Server documents itself (resources and tools)
nodes.rationale: Resources are usually user-attached so an agent will not discover them; a tool is already in its context. Both are drill-downs on purpose.

nodes.label: CI workflow (ci.yml)
nodes.rationale: Runs on every push and pull request on Windows and Linux (ADR-0007); Markdown changes run too because guides and skills are served at runtime and their tests read the real files.

nodes.label: Docs and skills served to clients at runtime
nodes.norm_label: docs and skills served to clients at runtime
nodes.rationale: The docs are part of the product, served as MCP resources and through readServerGuide/readSkill; guides.test.ts reads the real files so moving a doc without updating GUIDES fails the tests.

nodes.label: Small local model (128k window) as design target
nodes.norm_label: small local model (128k window) as design target
nodes.rationale: Reliability on the smallest client comes from better tools rather than more of them.

nodes.label: Composite tool
nodes.rationale: Call order, lock-handle lifetime, session binding and the obligation to unlock after a failure cannot be typed into schemas; a rule a model must remember across four calls is sometimes forgotten, and an orphaned lock on a shared system blocks other people.

nodes.label: ModManager seam (SKYRIM_MOD_MANAGER=mo2|amethyst)
nodes.rationale: Chosen by configuration, never inferred from the OS; tools are the same for every manager, with manager-specific detail only in their answers.

nodes.label: ADR-0001: The tool count is a cost, not a goal
nodes.norm_label: adr-0001: the tool count is a cost, not a goal
nodes.rationale: Measured, not aesthetic: every tool schema costs tokens on every turn for clients without on-demand schema fetching (~140 tools = ~19,000 tokens, full coverage ~51,000); the smallest client in scope, a local model with a 128k window, is the design target.

nodes.label: ADR-0002: Composite tools where the protocol is the hard part
nodes.norm_label: adr-0002: composite tools where the protocol is the hard part

nodes.label: Demand is the evidence for adding a tool
nodes.norm_label: demand is the evidence for adding a tool
nodes.rationale: A capability that genuinely blocks a real task justifies a tool; the backend's catalogue does not.

nodes.label: Tool set stays as small as the jobs it serves
nodes.norm_label: tool set stays as small as the jobs it serves
nodes.rationale: The backend's remaining surface is a source of improvements to existing tools (better arguments, fewer round trips, richer results), not a list of tools to build; coverage is a diagnostic, not a target.

nodes.label: Clean-up on every path, failures reported not thrown
nodes.norm_label: clean-up on every path, failures reported not thrown
nodes.rationale: A composite must leave the backend no worse than it found it; a clean-up failure must neither turn a successful write into an error nor mask the failure that caused it.

nodes.label: Ordering-and-obligations test for composites
nodes.rationale: A composite is justified when ordering and obligations are the hard part, not merely because calls are adjacent; not a licence to wrap every sequence.

nodes.label: One seam: Linux means Amethyst (rejected)
nodes.rationale: MO2 under Proton is a Linux setup too, and a second Linux manager would have to undo the assumption everywhere.

nodes.label: Tools per mod manager (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Twice the tools for the same jobs, and every skill would have to say which to call.

nodes.label: FileVersionInfo Fails for Native PE on Unix
nodes.norm_label: fileversioninfo fails for native pe on unix

nodes.label: PE RT_VERSION Parser
nodes.rationale: Prefer the StringFileInfo FileVersion and fall back to VS_FIXEDFILEINFO, because older Skyrim EXEs leave the fixed version at 1.0.0.0.

nodes.label: xEdit Has No Windowless Mode
nodes.rationale: SSEEdit is a Delphi VCL GUI; script and automation modes still open the main window and exit via -autoexit.

nodes.label: CI test job (unit and type tests)
nodes.norm_label: ci test job (unit and type tests)

nodes.label: Gating
nodes.rationale: Distinct from a tool profile: a profile is what the operator chose to offer, gating is what the backend can actually do.

nodes.label: Per-session bearer token (SKYRIM_ACCEPTED_TOKENS)
nodes.rationale: Each caller's token becomes that session's identity and one backend is built per session, so two people never share one credential; with no remote API behind it, the token list is the whole authority.

nodes.label: Local models through Ollama
nodes.rationale: Ollama defaults to a 4k context below 24 GiB VRAM; the model must make real tool calls (gemma4:26b and e4b do, code-completion models write calls as text).

nodes.label: Path settings read as a POSIX shell would
nodes.norm_label: path settings read as a posix shell would
nodes.rationale: Neither .env nor a client's env block passes through a shell, so ~ and variables are expanded by the server itself, relative paths taken from the server's folder; %VAR% and $(...) are refused.

nodes.label: Per-session rate limit (token bucket)
nodes.rationale: One agent in a loop looks exactly like healthy traffic from the front and can take a shared backend down for everyone.

nodes.label: Session bound to its token
nodes.rationale: A session id is a routing key, not a credential; only a digest of the token is kept.

nodes.label: TLS terminated in front of the server
nodes.norm_label: tls terminated in front of the server

nodes.label: Capability gate
nodes.rationale: Every failure path leaves the gate empty and the list complete: hiding a tool that would have worked is worse than offering one that errors, because the first is invisible.

nodes.label: Response and error model
nodes.rationale: A failed call is a result (isError) not an exception; one level of compact JSON, because indentation costs response budget and buys a model nothing.

nodes.label: Request lifecycle (tools/list, tools/call)
nodes.rationale: The router is derived from getTools(), so a tool cannot be listed without being callable.

nodes.label: Test suites (offline vitest)
nodes.rationale: Contract-suite arguments are generated from each tool's inputSchema, so a new tool is covered the moment it is listed.

nodes.label: ToolDefinition contract
nodes.rationale: narrowingHint and needsFeature live on the tool rather than in a table keyed by tool name, because such a table goes stale silently on a rename.

nodes.label: Errors must be McpError and name the next step
nodes.norm_label: errors must be mcperror and name the next step
nodes.rationale: A raw Error reaching the client becomes an opaque Internal error; a model reads the message and acts on it.

nodes.label: Single retry and permanent credential latch
nodes.norm_label: single retry and permanent credential latch
nodes.rationale: Only errors proving nothing was applied are retried, and only once; a refused credential is latched because every retry is another failed logon that can lock the account.

nodes.label: tools/list is the truth
nodes.rationale: A tool outside the profile is not callable and a withheld one is a backend property, so retrying either does not help.

nodes.label: Mutagen Binary Overlay Import Mode
nodes.rationale: Only fields that are accessed get parsed; the mod object returns almost immediately and the GC can free records; trade-off: repeated access re-parses.

nodes.label: GPL Mere Aggregation (separate processes)
nodes.rationale: Pipes, sockets and command-line arguments between separate programs normally keep them separate works, while linking makes a combined work; GPL code (Mutagen, libloot) is best kept in a separate process from the MIT server.

nodes.label: CETCompat false for MO2 Compatibility
nodes.rationale: MO2 does not play well with the .NET 9 CET feature, so the csproj sets CETCompat to false.

nodes.label: Mutagen Passthrough Correctness Tests
nodes.rationale: Import, re-export and byte-compare after normalisation to prove read/write correctness.

nodes.label: ICU Requirement (.NET globalization)
nodes.rationale: The helper is deliberately not globalization-invariant because Mutagen's YAML writer formats with the en culture; on Linux .NET fails to start without ICU.

nodes.label: Distribution frameworks (SPID, KID, SkyPatcher)
nodes.rationale: They change things at runtime from text files instead of overriding records, avoiding conflicts; prefer them for broad additions.

nodes.label: Mod order, files and archives (virtual Data, overwrite, profiles)
nodes.norm_label: mod order, files and archives (virtual data, overwrite, profiles)

nodes.label: Mod order decides files, load order decides records
nodes.norm_label: mod order decides files, load order decides records

nodes.label: Wabbajack
nodes.rationale: Warn before changing a Wabbajack-installed instance: list authors usually void support for modified installs, and an update deletes files the list does not know.

nodes.label: Spell fields (type, cast type, delivery, cost, half-cost perk)
nodes.norm_label: spell fields (type, cast type, delivery, cost, half-cost perk)

nodes.label: FaceGen files and the dark-face bug
nodes.norm_label: facegen files and the dark-face bug
nodes.rationale: The game loads pre-generated face files rather than building faces at runtime, so any appearance change needs regeneration in the Creation Kit; mod order and load order disagreeing causes dark faces.

nodes.label: The Creation Kit's role here (compiler only; pull after CK edits)
nodes.norm_label: the creation kit's role here (compiler only; pull after ck edits)
nodes.rationale: The server uses only what runs without the CK window (its Papyrus compiler); records are edited in the project. Render-window work and navmesh are the user's, after which the deployed plugin must be pulled back or the next deploy refuses to overwrite the CK's work.

nodes.label: Distribution (SPID) instead of NPC edits
nodes.rationale: Overrides conflict with every other mod touching those NPCs; SPID applies at runtime without overriding anything. Edit records only for specific NPCs.

nodes.label: Race, class, voice type
nodes.rationale: A new race or voice type lacks every vanilla armor addon, hair, dialogue condition and generic line, so prefer vanilla ones.

nodes.label: NPC templates and template flags
nodes.rationale: A field covered by a set template flag is ignored on the NPC itself - the most common 'my edit has no effect' on generic NPCs.

nodes.label: What a save keeps of an NPC
nodes.norm_label: what a save keeps of an npc

nodes.label: Appearance step: user generates FaceGen in the CK, copied into assets/
nodes.norm_label: appearance step: user generates facegen in the ck, copied into assets/

nodes.label: Race and voice table (Female flag beside a woman's voice)
nodes.norm_label: race and voice table (female flag beside a woman's voice)

nodes.label: Saves and SKSE co-saves (keep a copy before updating/disabling)
nodes.norm_label: saves and skse co-saves (keep a copy before updating/disabling)
nodes.rationale: A mod disabled mid-playthrough leaves orphaned traces and a mayNotWork DLL can corrupt a save silently, so the user keeps a copy of the latest save and tests on a copy.

nodes.label: Nexus gating exception (nexus-api-key, nexus-premium)
nodes.rationale: By the user's decision: Nexus tools need a key, and downloads need Nexus to confirm a premium account; an unanswered check withholds the download.

nodes.label: Nexus Mods API Generations (v1, v2, v3)
nodes.norm_label: nexus mods api generations (v1, v2, v3)

nodes.label: Nexus API Acceptable Use Policy
nodes.rationale: Personal keys are tolerated only for testing or personal use; public apps must register; no scraping, no stored user keys, no blank or impersonating metadata.

nodes.label: Adding a tool is a one-file change
nodes.norm_label: adding a tool is a one-file change
nodes.rationale: getTools(), the router, tools/list and the contract tests all derive from toolSpecs(), so a listed tool is always callable and always tested.

nodes.label: Linux setup with Amethyst
nodes.rationale: With Amethyst open, deploy asks for Refresh then Deploy, because deploying behind its window would race it.

nodes.label: Mod Organizer under Proton (experimental)
nodes.rationale: Deploy refuses while this instance's Mod Organizer runs, because MO2 holds the profile in memory and writes it back on exit and cannot be told to re-read it under Proton.

nodes.label: OpenClaw registration (skills, agent, workspace)
nodes.rationale: OpenClaw reads no server instructions and hides MCP tools behind Tool Search for a local model, so setup registers skills, an agent with thinking on and a workspace; behind Tool Search the agent took two to three times the turns.

nodes.label: Tool annotations (readOnly, destructive, idempotent, openWorld)
nodes.rationale: Hints, not a permission system: how a client decides what to auto-approve and what to put in front of a human.

nodes.label: healthcheck tool
nodes.rationale: Never connects to the backend, so it answers when nothing else does; defined in the server, listed in every profile.

nodes.label: Creation Kit
nodes.rationale: Stays for what only it can do (placing objects, navmesh); its work is pulled back into the text.

nodes.label: npm run setup (setup program)
nodes.rationale: Installs the .NET 10 SDK if missing, builds server and helper, finds the mod manager and asks only for what it cannot find, registers with Claude Code, Claude Desktop, VS Code and OpenClaw, ends with a healthcheck; asks before anything it installs, downloads or registers.

nodes.label: Papyrus compiler (Creation Kit's or russo-2025's)
nodes.rationale: The Creation Kit's compiler needs .NET Framework 3.5 on Windows and does not run on Linux, where russo-2025's papyrus-compiler is used.

nodes.label: Every tool declares a title and all four annotation hints
nodes.norm_label: every tool declares a title and all four annotation hints
nodes.rationale: OpenAI's directory rejects a tool omitting a hint, and a client falling back to the defaults treats a new search tool like a delete; annotations must also be true, checked by repeating calls.

nodes.label: A status code is not a diagnosis
nodes.norm_label: a status code is not a diagnosis
nodes.rationale: An unreachable backend, a refused credential and a missing permission can share one HTTP status yet need opposite fixes; health() lets the startup failure and healthcheck say which.

nodes.rationale: Build writes each new record's FormID back into the project; once assigned it never changes. Build, deploy and pull are explicit steps; nothing watches files.

nodes.rationale: Without pull, work done in the Creation Kit or xEdit would vanish on the next deploy. Pull refuses to write over uncommitted text; where git cannot answer it proceeds with a warning, since refusing would leave no way to pull.

nodes.rationale: Claude edits the text with its ordinary file tools, so the server needs far fewer tools, and git gives diff, review and rollback for free; the plugin is a build output.

nodes.rationale: A plugin saved by Bethesda's tools is normalised once on first pull (translation order, negative zeros, NumRecords/NextFormID) and stable after, so pull and deploy can compare text without false alarms.

nodes.rationale: Saves and other plugins point at a FormID, so renumbering or deleting and re-creating a record breaks every one of them.

nodes.rationale: What the server serves, the reference documents and the contract tests check must be one list; never keep a second.

nodes.label: Spriggit Translation Packages (NuGet)
nodes.rationale: Text output is stamped with package and version so old text deserialises with the old package; first use needs nuget.org and the .NET SDK.

nodes.label: CI helper build and check
nodes.rationale: Builds the plugin helper for each system and starts it once: checks its protocol and a version read from a version resource, which on Linux is the helper's own parser.

nodes.label: CI smoke test step
nodes.rationale: Drives the built server over real stdio and fails on anything but JSON-RPC frames on stdout, which no unit test can see; given a nonexistent SKYRIM_MO2_INSTANCE because a runner has no game, so it starts and healthcheck reports the instance unreadable.

nodes.label: Test instance (portable MO2 on a clean game, or throwaway Amethyst profile)
nodes.norm_label: test instance (portable mo2 on a clean game, or throwaway amethyst profile)
nodes.rationale: The server writes mod folders, mod order and load order; a Wabbajack-installed instance deletes every mod it did not install on its next update.

nodes.label: stdio transport
nodes.rationale: The backend is connected before the transport, so a wrong credential or unreachable backend fails at startup with a diagnosis on stderr rather than on the first tool call.

nodes.label: Never write to stdout
nodes.rationale: stdout carries MCP protocol frames over stdio; anything else corrupts the stream and breaks every tool at once. dotenv 17 did it, which is why index.ts loads it quiet.

nodes.label: Write paths run against a real backend once
nodes.norm_label: write paths run against a real backend once
nodes.rationale: A fake accepts any order of calls so it cannot know the backend's own rules; what is learned is then encoded as an assertion so the fake enforces it.

nodes.label: Papyrus Compiler Options on Linux (by fidelity)
nodes.norm_label: papyrus compiler options on linux (by fidelity)
nodes.rationale: No maintained byte-identical Linux compiler release exists today; ordered by fidelity: CK compiler in the prefix with .NET 3.5 or Mono, papyrusc 4.0 once released, russo's compiler now.

nodes.label: Claude Code Behind Ollama (tool search off, 4,096-char cut)
nodes.norm_label: claude code behind ollama (tool search off, 4,096-char cut)
nodes.rationale: Tool search is disabled behind a non-first-party ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, so every MCP tool loads upfront; the core profile and the response budget matter most there.

nodes.label: Ollama Default Context by VRAM
nodes.rationale: Default context is 4k below 24 GiB VRAM, so the server's instructions should not assume 64k.

nodes.label: oterm
nodes.rationale: stdio children inherit only six basic env vars, so server configuration must be declarable in env or a config file.

nodes.label: qwen2.5-coder:3b Writes Tool Calls as Text
nodes.norm_label: qwen2.5-coder:3b writes tool calls as text

nodes.label: Full Paths in addPatch/buildProject Answers
nodes.rationale: gemma4 joined plugin-relative file names to the project folder and failed every patch run; full paths in the answer gave the shortest route findRecords, addPatch, read_file, edit_file.

nodes.label: Flat Argument Schemas, No JSON-Schema Keyword Names
nodes.norm_label: flat argument schemas, no json-schema keyword names
nodes.rationale: gemma4 drops parameters named type/description/properties/required and oneOf arguments need coercion, so schemas stay flat with no root oneOf/anyOf.

nodes.label: No Terse local Tool Profile
nodes.rationale: The measured losses were not about the tool list; fixes that help every client (full paths, arguments sent as text taken as their declared type) went in for all.

nodes.label: Questions Only the Brother Can Answer

nodes.label: Amethyst Keeps Externally Added modlist Entries
nodes.norm_label: amethyst keeps externally added modlist entries
nodes.rationale: Each GUI save re-reads under a lock and prepends unknown lines, but writes known lines from memory, so an external flip or reorder of a known line is lost.

nodes.label: Safe Amethyst Write (new mod folder + prepend +Name)
nodes.norm_label: safe amethyst write (new mod folder + prepend +name)
nodes.rationale: Amethyst has no refresh IPC or watcher; add a new mod folder, prepend +Name and add *Plugin.esp, then the user presses Refresh and Deploy; never write into Data because restore moves unknown files to overwrite.

nodes.label: Three Bindings, One Shape (Windows MO2, MO2 under Proton, Amethyst)

nodes.rationale:
All three have mods/, overwrite/ and profiles/

/{modlist,plugins,loadorder}.txt; they differ only in where settings live (ModOrganizer.ini vs paths.json + deploy_state.json) and in * semantics.

nodes.rationale: Thinking off saved 41% of the time but lost 16 of 42 tasks (e4b 41/42 to 25/42); generated tokens, mostly thinking, are where the time goes.

nodes.rationale: On install or update every file the modlist does not account for is deleted, except downloads, saves and paths with a [NoDelete] component.

nodes.label: MO2 Overwrites External Edits on Exit
nodes.norm_label: mo2 overwrites external edits on exit
nodes.rationale: On exit MO2 writes modlist and plugin files from in-memory state; the safe external edit is to close MO2, edit and restart, or edit with no pending changes and immediately trigger refresh.

nodes.label: Editor-ID links resolved by the build (resolvedLinks)
nodes.norm_label: editor-id links resolved by the build (resolvedlinks)
nodes.rationale: A new record's FormKey line is never copied from another record, because that makes the file an override of the record it names.

nodes.norm_label: weapon kind table (mirror, animationtype, keyword, impactdataset)

nodes.norm_label: skill collection (directory of skill.md skills with supporting files)

nodes.label: A new spell names a vanilla effect
nodes.norm_label: a new spell names a vanilla effect
nodes.rationale: The effect is what the spell does and is shared by every spell naming it; strength is the spell's own Magnitude/Area/Duration. A new MGEF is only for what no vanilla effect does, and a vanilla MGEF changes only when everything using it should change.

nodes.label: Skill discovery (no rebuild, cached per process)
nodes.norm_label: skill discovery (no rebuild, cached per process)
nodes.rationale: Discovery walks each collection for SKILL.md files, so adding or editing one needs no rebuild; discoverSkills() caches the result per process, so a running server must be restarted to see changes.

nodes.label: Change examples only after building them against a test instance
nodes.norm_label: change examples only after building them against a test instance
nodes.rationale: Examples and table rows are verified by building them as written against a test instance; examples are kept unlike the eval-ollama authoring tasks so the eval measures a model working its record out of the tables rather than copying one.

nodes.label: Vanilla record/value tables in each SKILL.md
nodes.norm_label: vanilla record/value tables in each skill.md
nodes.rationale: Models read SKILL.md and seldom REFERENCE.md, so each SKILL.md holds one complete new record and tables of Skyrim.esm records; every table value is a Skyrim.esm record, so the tables say to write them without a search.

nodes.label: Mod Organizer overwrite-folder copy guard
nodes.rationale: A plugin copy the Creation Kit saves lands in the overwrite folder, which outranks the mod; deploy guards it like the mod's own and removes it once pulled so it cannot hide the next deploy.

nodes.label: Amethyst mod manager
nodes.rationale: Amethyst cannot be told to re-read its files and overwrites outside changes to modlist lines it knows, so deploy only adds what is new and runs Amethyst's own deploy when its window is closed, else asks the user to press Refresh and Deploy.

nodes.label: MO2 under Proton: path mapping and refused deploy
nodes.norm_label: mo2 under proton: path mapping and refused deploy
nodes.rationale: Windows paths in ModOrganizer.ini are mapped through the prefix's dosdevices links (SKYRIM_WINE_PREFIX, else MO2-LINT state.json, else Z: is /). MO2's refresh is not delivered into a Proton prefix, so a deploy is refused while that instance's MO2 runs; documented as unverified.

nodes.label: DelayedFileWriter 200 ms pending window
nodes.rationale: Refresh clobbers an external edit only if the user changed the mod list in MO2's UI less than 200 ms earlier; otherwise MO2 re-reads from disk.

nodes.label: MOMultiProcess: one primary MO2, commands forwarded
nodes.norm_label: momultiprocess: one primary mo2, commands forwarded
nodes.rationale: A second ModOrganizer.exe sends its command line to the system-wide primary, fire-and-forget; -p guards the profile but -i cannot tell two portable instances apart.

nodes.label: MO2 does not watch profile files
nodes.norm_label: mo2 does not watch profile files

nodes.label: Detect a running MO2 instance by process image path
nodes.norm_label: detect a running mo2 instance by process image path
nodes.rationale: MO2 creates no run-lock file; compare each ModOrganizer.exe's full image path with the instance directory; selected_profile in ModOrganizer.ini is only a hint.

nodes.label: MO2 overwrites external edits on launch and exit
nodes.norm_label: mo2 overwrites external edits on launch and exit
nodes.rationale: OrganizerCore::beforeRun and the destructor call saveCurrentProfile, so an external edit not followed by a refresh is lost when the user launches anything or closes MO2.

nodes.label: Plugin order chosen by mtime (loadorder.txt vs plugins.txt)
nodes.norm_label: plugin order chosen by mtime (loadorder.txt vs plugins.txt)
nodes.rationale: GamebryoGamePlugins::readPluginLists picks the order by mtime, so an external tool should write both files consistently, or write only plugins.txt and leave loadorder.txt older.

nodes.label: refresh launches the GUI when MO2 is not running
nodes.norm_label: refresh launches the gui when mo2 is not running
nodes.rationale: RefreshCommand::runPostOrganizer returns and main goes on to app.run(), so a tool must check MO2 is running before calling refresh.

nodes.label: Operating-system and mod-manager seams (ADR-0007)
nodes.rationale: What differs by operating system and by mod manager sits behind two separate seams; code that differs by system belongs only in platform.ts, and its Linux side is tested on Windows too.
